questions.evidence:
[Sessions] Cedar offers 9:00 and 10:00 starts; Maple offers 9:30 and 10:30 starts. Every session lasts thirty minutes, with an optional fifteen-minute discussion immediately afterward. Arrival must be at least five minutes before the start.

[Rae's limits] Rae can reach the building no earlier than 9:20. She must leave it by 10:20 to catch her train. She wants to complete both the timed session and the discussion if possible. All four sessions currently have a place available.

[Review option] Students unable to attend discussion can collect a printed explanation sheet. Its reasoning matches the discussion. Reservations are limited to one session, and changing a booking requires releasing the old place first.

Rae compares whole time blocks rather than start times alone. She finds a session that lets her arrive properly, finish both parts, and leave before her deadline. The availability of a seat matters, but it cannot make an unsuitable time fit her journey.
